newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Iraq admits to obtaining nerve gas in past.
newsitem.headline: Iraq admits to obtaining nerve gas in past.

text.p: Iraq has admitted to U.N. weapons inspectors that it had once acquired 3,800 kilograms of the nerve gas VX, according to British Ambassador John Weston on Monday, following a U.N. Security Council 60-day review of Iraqi sanctions.
Weston, quoting Rolf Ekeus, the head of the U.N. Special Commission in charge of destroying weapons of mass destruction, said this was one reason sanctions must be maintained against Iraq.
Weston said overall, the report from Ekeus was "gloomy," despite the fact some progress was made in recent weeks on giving missile engines to Ekeus' inspectors for analysis in the United States.
Ekeus has previously suspected Iraq took possession of large quantities of the nerve gas, but is still not certain how much destroyed or how much remained.

In mid 1995, Ekeus reported that his inspectors had been unable to account for some ingredients to produce at least 250 tonnes of a deadly nerve gas VX, which is 10 times deadlier than sarin, the agent used in the Tokyo subway. Iraq's claims it dumped the ingredients in the desert has not yet been checked.

Weston also said that on February 18, Iraq had agreed to allow the International Committee of the Red Cross to go to Iraq and speak to prisoners of war from the Gulf war, another requirement for lifting trade sanctions.

"So let us hope that what we have heard recently about a new mood of cooperation proves to be converted into facts. But as of now the position is as it has been in past reviews -- sanctions must be maintained," Weston said.
